review.rationale: The supplied Gold is an appropriate independent expectation for this pending-decision planning case. Repository identity, base commit, paired-case identity, REQ-001, AC-001–AC-003, and inspection-owner paths agree with the original specification. DEC-001 is material and explicitly unresolved: B must stop at decisions with requirement-decision-pending for DEC-001, without selecting OPT-1 from the conditional recommendation or publishing assignable tasks. Empty task and assignment expectations are therefore coherent, including with the empty team roster and absence of capability claims. Any fixed hypothetical C input is not a human Decision and cannot resolve this case. The supplied source shows normalization and truthy-first lookup in core/api.ts, shared by classic and mini forwarding factories; forwarding/export consumers are inspection owners, not mandatory edits. The proposed mini test is correctly identified as new. Build configuration supports generated declarations rather than separately maintained declaration owners. Test configuration distinguishes runtime/AOT tests from TypeScript checking. Gold and preview releaseInput fingerprints match across repository, source, team, decision inputs, prompts, model, sampling, budgets, and metric policy. The source-manifest digest is a separately named fingerprint, not assumed interchangeable with releaseInput.sourceDigest. The original specification's preparation-state fields do not override the supplied frozen preview. This is approval of the benchmark expectation, not execution readiness, task authorization, human confirmation, or candidate validation. I reviewed only the supplied data, used no tools, executed no code, and did not independently recompute Service-calculated digests.
